::: {.why}
The ten t-statistics you wrote down last night are the single most important cautionary result in applied time series, and you generated them yourself rather than reading about them.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Explain why the t-statistic in a spurious regression diverges rather than converging, in terms of what happens to the residual.
- Say what fraction of independent random walk pairs reject at 5 percent, and what the fix is.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Scale up last night's experiment to 1,000 replications and plot the distribution of the t-statistic. Report the rejection rate at the nominal 5 percent level. It will be somewhere around three quarters rather than one twentieth.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Diagnose it: plot the residuals from one of those regressions and their autocorrelation function. The residual is itself a random walk, so the standard error formula is estimating the wrong quantity, and the divergence follows from that rather than from anything mysterious.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Show the fix and its cost: rerun the regression on first differences and confirm the rejection rate returns to nominal. Then note what differencing destroyed, which is any long-run relationship there might have been, and which week 12 exists to recover.
:::
:::
